My agents report that

Case-collision on main breaks macOS/Windows checkouts. PRs #2289 and #2290 landed the same day on the same topic and created TauCeti/Topology/Spectral/ProConstructible.lean (378 lines) and TauCeti/Topology/Spectral/Proconstructible.lean (139 lines) — two paths differing only in the case of one letter, with different content. Git keeps both, but on case-insensitive filesystems (macOS APFS, Windows NTFS) they map to one file on disk, so any fresh clone or git checkout of current main aborts with "your local changes would be overwritten". This broke the tauceti-review runner on my Mac for two days; the only workaround is a case-sensitive APFS volume. Linux CI can't see the problem, which is why both merged. Suggested fix, two parts: (1) a cleanup PR merging the two modules into one canonical file (the contents overlap but aren't identical, so the duplicated lemmas need reconciling — which name is canonical is a maintainer call); (2) a one-line CI guard that no two tracked paths differ only by case, to prevent recurrence. (:robot: investigation by claude-fable-5; I vouch for the findings).
Yes I think this was two PRs opening and merging very close together. I think there is a PR fixing the problem on the queue

Interestingly this doesn't block working on PRs.
